docs.title: 📱 Android Interview Prep (2026 Edition)
docs.text: Welcome to the ultimate preparation guide for Android Developers. This resource is designed to take you from Junior to Senior/Staff level by covering everything from core fundamentals to complex system design and CI/CD pipelines.

docs.title: 📱 Fundamentals
docs.text: Master the core building blocks of the Android OS. * Lifecycle: Deep dives into Activity and Fragment states. * Components: Services, Broadcast Receivers, and Content Providers. * Manifest & Context: Understanding the app's blueprint and memory-safe context usage.

docs.title: 🧠 Kotlin
docs.text: Modern Android is Kotlin-first. We cover language internals and idiomatic usage. * Core: Null safety, Extension functions, and Higher-order functions. * Advanced: Inline functions, Reified types, and Sealed Class hierarchies. * Asynchronous: Coroutines and Flow (StateFlow/SharedFlow).

docs.title: 🛠️ Jetpack Compose
docs.text: The declarative UI standard for Android. * State: remember, rememberSaveable, and State Hoisting. * Internals: Recomposition cycles and stability. * Effects: Managing side effects with LaunchedEffect and DisposableEffect.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text: Design patterns that define professional, scalable apps. * Patterns: MVVM, MVI, and Clean Architecture. * DI: Hilt, Dagger2, and Koin. * Scalability: Modularization strategies and the Repository pattern.

docs.title: ⚡ Concurrency
docs.text: Efficient background processing. * Coroutines: Dispatchers, Scopes, and Structured Concurrency. * Flow vs LiveData: Migration strategies and use cases. * Threading: Handlers, Loopers, and the Main Thread.

docs.title: 🌐 Networking & Offline
docs.text: Data persistence and API communication. * Networking: Retrofit, OkHttp, and Interceptors. * Database: Room, Migrations, and Relationships. * Strategy: Offline-First Architecture and data synchronization.

docs.title: 🚀 Performance & Vitals
docs.text: Building "buttery smooth" experiences. * Optimization: Memory leaks (LeakCanary), ANRs, and App Startup time. * Metrics: App Vitals and Play Console performance tracking. * Debugging: Profilers, Logcat, and StrictMode.

docs.title: ⚙️ CI/CD & Release
docs.text: The "DevOps" of Android. * Pipelines: GitHub Actions and automated workflows. * Management: Release Strategies, App Bundles, and Gradual Rollouts.

docs.title: 🏗️ System Design
docs.text: Senior-level discussions on building complex systems. * Designing Image Loaders (Glide/Coil). * Real-time Chat and Feed systems. * Analytics and Logging SDKs.

docs.title: 🎓 Advanced & Security
docs.text: Going deep into the OS. * Internals: AOSP basics and Binder IPC. * Security: Keystore, ProGuard, and R8. * Form Factors: Foldables and Tablets.

docs.title: 🎯 Goal of This Project
docs.text: This project aims to create a practical Android interview preparation resource with: - Interview-Focused Answers: Not just documentation, but how to explain it to an interviewer. - 2026 Standards: Focused on Compose, KMP, and On-device AI. - Real Examples: Code snippets that actually work in production.

docs.title: Cicd Pipelines
docs.text:
Key Interview Concept

Interviewers love asking about automation and how you ensure code quality before a release.

docs.title: 🏗️ Pipeline Stages
docs.text:
1. Linting: Checking for code style and static analysis.
  2. Unit Tests: Ensuring logic works as expected.
  3. Build: Generating the .aab (Android App Bundle).
  4. UI Tests: Running Espresso/Compose tests on a device farm.
  5. Deploy: Uploading to the Play Store Internal track.
